newsitem.title: CONGO: Mandela leaves Congo after Zaire talks cancelled.
newsitem.headline: Mandela leaves Congo after Zaire talks cancelled.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela left the Congo for home late on Wednesday after failing to broker a second round of talks between Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and his rebel rival, Laurent Kabila, a spokesman said.
A South African Foreign Ministry spokesman said Mandela left after discussing with Mobutu the rebel leader's failure to arrive for the shipboard meeting.

United Nations envoy Mohamed Sahnoun announced earlier on Wednesday that Kabila had refused to board a South African navy ice-breaker for talks with Mobutu unless the vessel sailed into international waters. Mandela rejected the demand.

Officials on the ship had said they expected Mandela to address a news conference after consulting Mobutu, but Foreign Ministry spokesman Marco Boni told reporters the president flew home, leaving an aide to brief the media.
Sahnoun said Mandela and the U.N. would not give up their efforts to broker a second face-to-face meeting between Mobutu and Kabila, who met for the first time on the South African ship 10 days ago.

South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki said on Tuesday the talks, which were to have started at 11 a.m. (1000 GMT), could be the last chance to avoid a bloodbath in the streets of the Zairean capital Kinshasa.
